term: bounded resource increase, finite duration and pointwise versus uniform positive growth
resolution: The new constraint bounds resource spread S(now)−L, not elapsed time or the number of past events. Integer time is beginningless by the chosen profile; no traversal from a first event or finite-duration budget is assumed. PositiveStep and UniformPastGrowth use one fixed epsilon across ALL past steps, unlike a positive step-dependent increase. An exponential stock can be strictly increasing with no such uniform positive minimum while remaining lower-bounded on the past; linear stock has uniform unit growth but no past lower bound. The result compares these arithmetic assignments, not their physical realizability. Stock remains neutral; interpreting it as entropy requires additional dynamics and domain justification, not a relabeling of the theorem. Causal well-foundedness, modal necessity and timeless eternity are different questions.
